# Decisions (ADR log)

When the Product Owner decides an approach, a trade-off, a scope cut or a rule, add an ADR to `compass/spec.json → decisions` in the same PR.

## ADR-001 · Compass follows its own delivery process

_2026-11-26 · Accepted · REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004_

**Context:** Compass enforced the AI-native SDLC in other repos but not on its own code.

**Decision:** The Product Owner approved the intent: Compass's own repo gets the Compass Framework generated by the portal itself, CI on every pull request, tests for the checking scripts and a no-drift check between compass/ and src/framework/.

**Consequences:** Every later Compass PR needs an approved intent, approved requirements, a design (or none: <reason>), a plan file and an independent review. The setup PR is larger than 12 files because the check does not exist on main yet.

## ADR-002 · Light baseline for the existing portal

_2026-11-26 · Accepted_

**Context:** The portal existed before its repo had a spec.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose a light baseline: one feature per stage (F-001…F-007) with one Done requirement each (REQ-101…107); detailed requirements are written only for new work.

**Consequences:** Older behaviour is documented at stage level only; new work starts at REQ-001.

## ADR-003 · Team floor is a live view of the existing run trace

_2026-11-26 · Accepted · REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009_

**Context:** The Product Owner asked for a realtime "creative team" interface like those other AI users built.

**Decision:** The Product Owner approved the intent for option 1: a Team floor page drawn only from the run trace Compass already records. Agents talking to each other and multi-device viewing are out of scope, each needing its own decision.

**Consequences:** No change to agents, tools, guardrails or approval gates; no extra Claude cost; live only in the browser tab that runs the agents.

## ADR-004 · Compass shares the Bee There honey brand on every page

_2026-11-26 · Accepted · REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012_

**Context:** The Team floor design was drawn in a new Figma file; the Product Owner asked for the Bee There look with its signature honey yellow.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose to rebrand all Compass pages (not only the Team floor) to the Honey edition of the design system in the Figma file "Compass — Team floor", which becomes the project design tool. Honey means brand and "your turn"; working moves from amber/teal to sky so the two never look alike.

**Consequences:** The teal theme is retired; the colour tokens in src/index.css follow the Figma variables; a test keeps old teal out of src/. Where Bee There's text colours fall below WCAG AA 4.5:1 (grey #8A8072, brand text #A87400, and the state texts on pale honey), Compass uses one shade darker; the Product Owner approved this on 2026-11-26.

## ADR-005 · Intents say "Done when"; a baseline and target only for bets

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-020, REQ-021_

**Context:** The Ideation agent asked every business intent for "baseline → target, by when" and invented numbers with no data behind them (e.g. "0% → 20% within 90 days" for a Bee There feature). The Product Owner found them hard to judge.

**Decision:** The Product Owner decided on 2026-11-27 (same rule as travel-map ADR-021): every intent has a "Done when" in plain words. A small feature may add one optional signal to watch without a target; a process change has "Done when" only; only a change she names a bet gets a metric with its current value, and its target is set after a few weeks of real data. The Ideation agent never invents a baseline or target.

**Consequences:** The Ideation agent prompt, its offline draft, the installed framework text and the Idea page change; the stored field outcomeMetric keeps its name so existing briefs need no migration. Existing briefs keep their text until the agent is re-run.

## ADR-006 · Quote and revise: every agent, with versions

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-050, REQ-051, REQ-052, REQ-053, REQ-054_

**Context:** F-020 lets the reviewer quote part of an agent answer and Ask or Revise. Two scope questions came up before the requirements were written.

**Decision:** The Product Owner decided in chat on 2026-11-27: (1) every agent can be quoted and revised, including the coding agent, whose revision re-proposes only the quoted files; (2) a revision creates versions v1, v2… with a compare view, and Approve always applies the latest version. A revision may change only the quoted items; anything else is refused.

**Consequences:** Runs keep a conversation and their versions. A revised version waits for its guardrails before it can be approved. The Ask and Revise of live runs cost Claude tokens, shown per answer.

## ADR-007 · Figma file layout: one Components page, one section per feature

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-025_

**Context:** Components were spread over the prototype, design-system and feature pages of the "Compass — Team floor" Figma file, and feature screens lay loose on the canvas, which made reviews hard to follow.

**Decision:** The Product Owner decided in chat on 2026-11-27: every Figma component lives on the "Components" page, and each feature gets one Figma section holding all its screens, for this and every future feature. Same rule as travel-map REQ-061 / ADR-022.

**Consequences:** Existing components were moved (instances left where they were shown) and existing feature screens grouped; node ids are unchanged, so frame links still work. The design template Compass installs states the rule; CI cannot read Figma, so it is not checked automatically.

## ADR-010 · Team access uses Firebase on the free Spark plan

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-030, REQ-032, REQ-033, REQ-035_

**Context:** Compass is a browser-only app without a server. Team lists and role checks must be shared between people and cannot be trusted if they live only in each browser.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose Firebase Auth (Google sign-in) and Firestore on the free Spark plan, with Firestore security rules as the real gate, over a team.json file in each repo or browser-only storage.

**Consequences:** New dependency firebase and a firestore rules file (both need the human-approved label); the Product Owner creates the Firebase project and publishes the rules once; ideas, runs and other data stay where they are.

## ADR-011 · Members use a shared GitHub token per project

_2026-11-27 · Superseded by ADR-016 · REQ-034, REQ-031_

**Context:** GitHub writes need a token. Team members who sign in with Google may have no GitHub account or token.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose one GitHub token per project, stored by its Admins and readable by its members, over each member connecting their own token.

**Consequences:** Every member's browser can read the token (the Team page only hides it from non-Admins), so a member could copy it and could also commit to the repo without the portal's role checks (see ADR-012); removing them does not revoke that copy. Mitigation: the portal asks for a fine-grained token for that repo only (Contents, Pull requests, Issues) with an expiry date, and reminds Admins to replace it after removing someone.

## ADR-012 · Approvals are recorded in Firebase and unconfirmed ones are flagged

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-033, REQ-036, REQ-037, REQ-038_

**Context:** The independent review of PR #74 found that approvals are commits of spec.json made with the shared project token, so Firestore rules never see them: any member could commit an approval for a gate their role does not own, or forge approvedBy.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose to write every approval to Firestore first (the rules accept it only from the signed-in person's own verified email and a role they hold that owns the gate, or "super admin" for the account in config/access, and records cannot be changed or deleted), commit to GitHub only after that, and flag approvals in spec.json that have neither a matching record nor a place in the baseline stored by the super admin together with the project's first team (only the super admin can create a first team) (dates in the repo are not trusted) — over accepting screen-only checks or going back to personal tokens.

**Consequences:** Two more requirements (REQ-037, REQ-038). A member with the token can still edit spec.json directly, but such approvals show as Unconfirmed. Known limit: a record names the item and gate, not its content, so editing the text of an already approved item keeps it confirmed; a content fingerprint could be added later. The updated design (Unconfirmed badge) was approved on 2026-11-27. Residual risk: an approval forged into spec.json before the team is first created goes into the baseline and is never flagged.

## ADR-013 · The super admin is recorded automatically at first sign-in

_2026-11-27 · Changed by ADR-018 · REQ-035_

**Context:** The Product Owner asked not to add herself to Firestore by hand. Writing her email into the rules would publish a personal email in the repo.

**Decision:** The Firestore rules hold a SHA-256 hash of the super admin's lower-case Google email. When that account signs in for the first time, the portal creates config/access with it; the rules allow that create only for a matching hash and refuse any later change from a browser.

**Consequences:** No manual Firestore step. Adding or changing a super admin later means a rules change (new hash) or an edit in the Firebase console. A hash of an email can be guessed by trying likely emails, so it hides the address from casual readers only.

## ADR-014 · With sign-in, roles come from the team; the role picker lives on only in the demo

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-039, REQ-040_

**Context:** The onboarding screen "What's your role?" lets anyone pick a role. With Google sign-in the admin sets roles, so picking one would contradict the team; but the live site would then lose its demo.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose: with sign-in on, roles come only from the team and the role screen is not shown; a signed-in person can open a demo (sample projects in the browser only), where they pick a role as today — offered on the no-access screen and in the sidebar account menu.

**Consequences:** No new screen for the role picker (the existing onboarding screen is reused inside the demo). The demo must never read or write Firebase, GitHub or real projects (TC-076).

## ADR-015 · Project design files live on a new Project settings page

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-080, REQ-081, REQ-082_

**Context:** The first design put the project's Figma and Miro links on the Feature board; the Product Owner found that page unsuitable for them.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose in chat on 2026-11-27: a "Project settings" link with a gear icon is added to the sidebar's project group, for every role. Its page holds the "Design files" card; only the project admin edits it, others see the links with Open ↗. Follow-up decisions in chat, after Team access (F-015) and REQ-075 reached main: (1) the admin is the project's Admin or the super admin when sign-in is on, and the PO role from the role picker when sign-in is off (demo, local use); (2) Project settings is the last link: after Release, and after Team access's Admin-only Team link, which stays a separate item.

**Consequences:** REQ-070, REQ-075 and their tests list Project settings as the last project link. The Admin check is a portal check only: compass/spec.json → designTool lives in the repository, so anyone with GitHub write access can still change it there (Firestore rules never see GitHub commits).

## ADR-019 · "Try the demo" leaves the sidebar; account actions move into an account menu

_2026-11-28 · Accepted · REQ-110, REQ-073, REQ-039, REQ-040, REQ-032_

**Context:** The sidebar footer had four loose rows (account card, "Try the demo" and "Sign out" buttons, a "My roles" line and a lone theme button). The Product Owner asked to redesign it and reviewed a mockup in chat.

**Decision:** The Product Owner approved the mockup on 2026-11-28 with one change: "Remove try the demo in this section, the rest is fine to proceed". The footer is one account card (initial, name, role chips) that opens a menu with the email, Connections, the theme switch, Leave demo (in the demo) and Sign out.

**Consequences:** REQ-073: AC1 changes — clicking the account card opens the account menu, and "Connections" is an item in it; AC2 changes — the theme is a "Dark theme" switch in the menu and the role picker shows only with sign-in off or in the demo. REQ-039 AC2: the read-only roles show as chips on the account card instead of a "My roles: …" line (still read-only). REQ-032 AC2: the card shows the part of the email before "@"; the full email is in the card's tooltip and at the top of the account menu. REQ-040 AC2: signed-in people on a team no longer start the demo from the sidebar; "Try the demo" stays on the "You have no access yet" screen. TC-404 checks the theme switch and the Connections item in the menu.

## ADR-016 · Phase 1: everyone works through a shared GitHub work token set by super admins; project tokens are retired; only super admins create projects

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-041, REQ-042, REQ-043, REQ-044_

**Context:** Project Admins could set their own project token (ADR-011), and members could use their own tokens to import repositories. The Product Owner wants to control all GitHub access in phase 1.

**Decision:** The Product Owner decided in chat on 2026-11-27: "the intention is that everyone will use my personal token for action and changes in the first phase. So the github and anthropic token should only be configured by me". With sign-in on, Compass uses a fine-grained work token set by super admins (Compass project repositories only; Contents, Pull requests, Issues, Workflows and Pages: Read and write; Actions: Read; never Administration) for every team member on team projects; project tokens are retired. After the review of #117 the Product Owner chose (2026-11-28) that only super admins create or import projects, with a creator token kept only on their own device, so the shared work token, made as listed, never needs the rights to create or delete repositories. Every commit and pull request ends with "Made in Compass by <email> (<role>)" (the Product Owner kept the email). Supersedes ADR-011. Phase 2 (each person's own token, "Connect with GitHub") is on the backlog, #111.

**Consequences:** GitHub shows the work token owner's account on every change; the audit line helps reading but is not proof (the Firestore rules never see GitHub), Compass's approval records stay the proof. Every member's browser can read the work token, so it is limited and replaced when someone leaves. Members' emails become part of GitHub history, public in public repositories. A super admin adds each new repository to the work token on GitHub. One work token reaches every Compass project repository, and members of any team can read it, so a member of one project could change another project's repository on GitHub outside Compass; the Product Owner accepted this for phase 1 (chat, 2026-11-28: "Accept for phase 1"). One work token per project is in phase 2 (#111). Who can read the work token and key follows team membership, which project Admins set: adding someone gives their browser the token and key ("Accept: Admins are trusted", 2026-11-28). Compass cannot check from outside that the work token has no Administration permission ("Full list + reminder", 2026-11-28). After a project is created or imported, its setup waits until the work token reaches the new repository ("Wait for work token", 2026-11-28). Switching GitHub Pages on needs Administration, so it uses a super admin's creator token ("Creator token", 2026-11-28). Compass cannot check how the work token was made on GitHub; the protection holds only if it is made as listed.

## ADR-017 · Phase 1: everyone's live agents use the Anthropic key set by super admins

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-041_

**Context:** Live agent runs cost money on the key owner's Anthropic account.

**Decision:** The Product Owner decided in chat on 2026-11-27 (same message as ADR-016): with sign-in on, only super admins set the Anthropic key, and Compass uses it for every team member's live agent runs on team projects; a key saved on a member's device is not used.

**Consequences:** All agent cost is on the key owner's Anthropic account; every member's browser can read the key, so it gets its own spending limit and is replaced when someone leaves. Members use the model the super admins chose.

## ADR-018 · The owner can make other people super admins (changes ADR-013)

_2026-11-27 · Accepted · REQ-046, REQ-041_

**Context:** ADR-013 recorded a single super admin at first sign-in and allowed no change from a browser. In phase 1 the token and key must be manageable by more than one trusted person.

**Decision:** The Product Owner decided in chat on 2026-11-27: "Me and users given super admin permission can update the token". The owner (the hashed email in firestore.rules, ADR-013) can add or remove super admins on the Users screen; the owner can never be removed. Super admins can do everything except grant or remove super admin. Changes ADR-013's rule that no browser can change config/access: from now on the owner's browser can change its list.

**Consequences:** The Firestore rules let the owner update config/access; more people can see every project and read and replace the token and key.

## ADR-020 · With sign-in on, Connections is only for super admins, also in the account menu

_2026-11-28 · Accepted · REQ-041, REQ-110_

**Context:** REQ-110 (#119) put "Connections" in every signed-in person's account menu, while REQ-041 hides Connections from everyone but super admins.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose in chat on 2026-11-28: "Hide for members". With sign-in on, the account menu shows "Connections" only to super admins; REQ-110 AC2 is amended. With sign-in off or in the demo, as REQ-110 says.

**Consequences:** Members' account menu has their email, Dark theme and Sign out (and Leave demo in the demo).

## ADR-021 · Every GitHub issue follows a standard template: Figma link, screenshot and a detailed requirement table

_2026-11-28 · Accepted_

**Context:** Requirement issues were free text (story + Given/When/Then), with no link to the design and no picture, so readers had to open spec.json and Figma to understand them.

**Decision:** The Product Owner asked in chat on 2026-11-28: "for each github issue created, especially new requirement, attach the figma link and screenshot and provide a table of detailed requirement as standard template". .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/requirement.md and bug.md hold the standard; agents follow it for every issue they create (AGENTS.md). Screenshots are exported from the Figma frame, committed to compass/design/screens/ and linked by commit SHA.

**Consequences:** Every requirement issue shows its Figma frame, a screenshot, a Requirement details table and an Acceptance criteria table. A requirement without UI says "Design: none: <reason>".

## ADR-023 · The Design agent draws screens in Figma through a Compass Figma plugin, not Figma's MCP server

_2026-11-28 · Accepted · REQ-114, REQ-115, REQ-116, REQ-117, REQ-118, REQ-119, REQ-120_

**Context:** The Product Owner wants the Design stage to produce real Figma screens for review. A spike drew F-001 SCR-1 well through Figma's MCP server from Claude Code, but Figma lets only clients in its MCP catalog connect: registering Compass returned 403, and the Claude API's MCP connector is not in the catalog. Intent 2026-11-27-project-design-files.md had put writing Figma content out of scope.

**Decision:** The Product Owner chose in chat on 2026-11-28 ("go with 2b"): a Compass Figma plugin, kept in this repository, with the Design agent inside. The plugin calls Claude with the project's shared Anthropic key, draws with a fixed set of drawing tools (no tool runs code), checks images of its screens, and saves the frame links to compass/spec.json through the shared work token. The plugin signs in to Compass, and only UX, PO or Admin can draw. Compass stays browser-only with no server. This replaces "writing Figma content" in that intent's Out of scope.

**Consequences:** Compass has a second small app (the plugin) with its own build and tests. Everyone who can run the plugin can read the shared Anthropic key on their machine. Firestore rules guard who can read the key and token; they do not see the plugin's GitHub commits (ADR-016) or its Figma edits (Figma file permissions do). A Full Figma seat is needed to draw outside drafts. If Figma later accepts Compass in its MCP catalog, the plugin's tools can be swapped for the MCP server.
